research.facts:
CPSC Recalls — Magnet Toys and Battery Toys
**Sources consulted:**
- CPSC.gov: "Gagaku Children's Ice Cream Toy Playsets Recalled Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Magnet Ingestion Hazard; Violate Mandatory Standard for Toys; Sold on Amazon by Brandworl.USA"
- CPSC.gov: "ABC Trading Recalls Children's Toys Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Battery Ingestion; Violates Mandatory Standard for Toys"
- foodpoisoningbulletin.com: "ABC Trading Children's Toys Recalled For Battery Ingestion Hazard"
- St. Kitts and Nevis Bureau of Standards: "ABC Trading Recalls Children's Toys..."
- WLT Report (Aug 18, 2026): "Popular Toy Recalled After Multiple Kids Hospitalized With Life-Threatening Injuries"
**Verified facts — Gagaku/Brandworl.USA (HIGH — CPSC.gov official):**
- Product: Gagaku Children's Ice Cream Toy Playsets — confirmed CPSC.gov
- Hazard: magnet ingestion; magnets can cause perforations, twisting, blockage of intestines, blood poisoning, death — confirmed CPSC.gov
- Sold on Amazon by Brandworl.USA — confirmed CPSC.gov
- High-powered magnets can become lodged in digestive system — confirmed CPSC.gov
**Verified facts — ABC Trading (HIGH — CPSC.gov official):**
- Products: Toy Headband (model 6300RP, pink with white polka dots, push button on bow); Electronic Pet Cage-Dinosaur Tribes (model 8266/ZH998-22, silver cage with blue bottom); My Pet Bird Cute Bird Tribes (ZH998-23, pink top and bottom with blue bird) — confirmed CPSC.gov
- Hazard: button cell batteries in accessible compartments; ingestion causes serious injuries, internal chemical burns, death — confirmed CPSC.gov
- Sold: TOYZ and Joissu Product stores nationwide, November 2022–October 2025, $5–$9 — confirmed CPSC.gov
- Remedy: stop use immediately, contact ABC Trading for refund — confirmed CPSC.gov
**Note:** JINHEZO Mini Waterproof LED Tea Lights and OKK Trading LED Headbands (Aug 20, 2026) were covered in Aug 22 pipeline. Vevor Baby Swings + Delightmi/POPOOO Finger Lights were covered in Aug 16 pipeline. Gagaku and ABC Trading are new and not previously covered.

research.facts:
Paid Paternity Leave and Baby Health
**Sources consulted:**
- STAT News (Aug 17, 2026): "Paid paternity leave is critical for babies' health"
- Medical Xpress / Northwestern Now (June 2026): "Paid paternal leave linked to better mental health outcomes for dads"
- Northwestern University / Lurie Children's Hospital study (June 2026) — analyzed Ohio Fatherhood Survey 2022-2023
- AAP Pediatrics journal: "Impacts of Paid Family Leave on Perinatal Health: A Nationwide Quasi-Experimental Study" — analyzed 11,452,411 live singleton births, 2016–2022
- news-medical.net (June 18, 2026): "Paid paternity leave supports new fathers' mental health, study finds"
- Healio: "Paternal leave improves mental health among new fathers"
- contemporarypediatrics.com: "Study: Longer fathers' work leave improves breastfeeding duration"
**Verified facts (HIGH — multiple sources):**
- STAT News Aug 17, 2026 reported: paid paternity leave is critical for babies' health — confirmed
- Northwestern/Lurie study: fathers without paid leave face higher anxiety and depression — confirmed multiple sources
- AAP Pediatrics quasi-experimental study: analyzed 11.4M births; paid family leave policies improve perinatal outcomes — confirmed AAP Pediatrics abstract
- Fathers average 3 days vs mothers' 7.2 weeks after birth — confirmed news-medical.net (National Parent Survey data)
- Growing evidence fathers make independent contributions to child health — confirmed multiple sources
**Verified facts (MEDIUM — single source):**
- Ohio Fatherhood Survey 2022-2023 was the data source for Northwestern study — news-medical.net only
- 2026 National Parent Survey found the 3 days/7.2 weeks comparison — need to confirm which specific source
